title: Dev identity auth redirect and origin compatibility
summary: Static development identity and the live active public OAuth client registration both contain the exact development Chromium callback. The general Auth redirect allowlist omits that callback, but source confirms this OAuth flow uses the OAuth client's redirect_uris exact-match registration; the general list is not the applicable check. Actual browser sign-in remains unverified.

source_facts.oauth_flow: Supabase OAuth 2.1 public PKCE client; chrome.identity.getRedirectURL() is sent as redirect_uri

observed_live_auth_config.method: GET https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/{ref}/config/auth using existing SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN from ../aidream/.env in a process-only Authorization header; response parsed in memory and only URL configuration fields emitted

observed_oauth_client_registration.method: Supabase MCP read-only SQL: information_schema column discovery, then SELECT id, redirect_uris, client_type, (deleted_at IS NULL) AS active from auth.oauth_clients WHERE id matches source WXT_EXTENSION_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID; client_secret_hash was never selected

limitations: No browser sign-in/callback was exercised because the Mac is locked; this confirms registration readiness, not successful authentication.
Frontend origin compatibility here covers manifest/runtime origins and general auth URL config only; the extension OAuth callback itself is the chromiumapp URI.
sources: Supabase OAuth 2.1 exact client redirect URI rule (official docs: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/oauth-server/getting-started)
Supabase MCP read-only query of auth.oauth_clients registration columns for source WXT_EXTENSION_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
